The file holds the delay of a hover open for the store of Base UI. `Popover.Trigger` has the default `300` of its `delay` prop.

`Popover.test.ts` tests the root through the parts: the open state with each reason, `v-model:open` and `v-model:trigger-id`, `cancel()`, the stack of popovers, the dismissal, the modal state, the focus, the hover and the placement. The parts render no transition status and no unmount action: `<Transition>` animates the popup and the backdrop, and its JavaScript hooks replace `unmount()`, `preventUnmountOnClose()` and `openChangeComplete`.
`Popover.test.ts` tests the handle: triggers outside the root, `open(id)`, `close()`, `isOpen`, the payload of each trigger, an unknown id and a handle with no root.

`Popover.test.ts` tests the trigger: its element and attributes, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `data-pressed`, a disabled trigger, a disabled fieldset, Enter and Space on an element that is not a button, and the hover. `[aria-expanded="true"]` replaces `data-popup-open`, and `:disabled` replaces `data-disabled`.

`Popover.test.ts` tests the popup: its element and attributes, the first focus, `initialFocus` and `finalFocus`, the return of the focus, the Tab order and the error with no root. A lost focus moves nowhere: the next Tab goes on from its place (test/measurements/popup.test.ts). A popup in a toolbar needs no code of its own.

`Popover.test.ts` tests a popup in a `<Transition>`: the leave classes, and one popup element for an open while the old one leaves. The parts render no transition status and no unmount action: `<Transition>` animates the popup and the backdrop, and its JavaScript hooks replace `unmount()`, `preventUnmountOnClose()` and `openChangeComplete`.

`Popover.test.ts` tests the positioner: the side and the alignment, a side of the text direction, the variables, the transform origin, the scroll lock of a modal popover and a trigger that leaves the DOM.

`Popover.test.ts` tests the portal: `keepMounted`, the target of the portal above, `to` of `null` and `disabled`. The portal renders no element for `render` and `className`: its content goes to the target, and its only element in place is the visually hidden element that owns the popup.

`Popover.test.ts` tests the backdrop: its element, `hidden` and `inert` with `keepMounted`, `pointer-events: none` after a hover open, and a press on the backdrop of a child popover. The parts render no transition status and no unmount action: `<Transition>` animates the popup and the backdrop, and its JavaScript hooks replace `unmount()`, `preventUnmountOnClose()` and `openChangeComplete`.
`Popover.test.ts` tests the arrow: its element, `aria-hidden` and the attributes of its side.
`Popover.test.ts` tests the close button: a press closes with `close-press`, a disabled button closes nothing, and a modal popover keeps the focus only with a close button.
`Popover.test.ts` tests the title: the popup has its id in `aria-labelledby`, and an attribute of the developer wins.
`Popover.test.ts` tests the description: the popup has its id in `aria-describedby`.

`Popover.test.ts` tests the viewport: the direction of a move, and content in a `<Transition>` with the `triggerId` of the slot as its key, which leaves while the new content enters. That `<Transition>` replaces `data-current` and `data-previous`.
`Popover.spec.ts` tests the types of the handle, the details, the props of the root, the trigger and the positioner, and the element of a template ref.
`Popover.spec.ts` tests the types of the handle, the details, the props of the root, the trigger and the positioner, and the element of a template ref.
`@after-enter` and `@after-leave` of a `<Transition>` around the popup run after its animations.
A template ref of the root has `close()`. With `:css="false"`, the `leave` hook of a `<Transition>` keeps the popup until it calls `done`, so the root has no `unmount` action.
The trigger reads the element that it renders, so it has no `nativeButton`.
The button reads the element that it renders, so it has no `nativeButton`.

The portal is a `<Teleport>`: its content goes to the target, and its only element in place is the visually hidden element that owns the popup. So it has no `as` and no `element` slot. Put an element in the portal when you need one.

`<Transition>` around the backdrop animates it, so the state has no `transitionStatus`, and the backdrop has no `data-starting-style` and no `data-ending-style`. CSS selects a closed backdrop that stays in the DOM with `[hidden]`, so the backdrop has no `data-open` and no `data-closed`.

`<Transition>` around the popup animates it, so the state has no `transitionStatus`, and the popup has no `data-starting-style` and no `data-ending-style`. CSS selects a closed popup that stays in the DOM with `[hidden]`, so the popup has no `data-open` and no `data-closed`.
